Ascent Collection · Hero Film · Treatment v2

TheKeeper

A private museum at night. A man who kept the story. The archive that comes alive when he tells it.

Prepared for Terry & Reg Voice-over & score: locked, unchanged Everything you see: rebuilt

Why we're rebuilding it

The first cut was slides. This is a film.

The draft proved the spine works — the voice-over and the orchestral score carry real weight. But the picture was still images with slow pushes and a caption track. It looked like something anyone could make in an afternoon, and the framing literally cut people off.

The idea

Some stories should never fade. So we don't put the collection on a table — we build the room it lives in, and let a man who remembers hand it to someone who'll carry it on.

The character

The Keeper

A distinguished Caribbean gentleman, a veteran's bearing and a curator's poise. Dark three-piece, a poppy pin, a signet ring; reading glasses he removes to look straight at us. He is the voice-over given a body — the storyteller. At the very end, a younger hand enters the frame to receive the box: a legacy you can pass on.

The Keeper is a character we author, so we generate him freely. The real airmen, the Tuskegee pilots, Lena Horne and Mona Baptiste are honoured through their actual archival photographs, animated — never fabricated.

The world

The Personalised Museum

A private, lamplit gallery after hours — the Churchill War Rooms crossed with a Cartier salon. Deep navy shadows, pools of brass picture-light, glass vitrines glowing. A Rolls-Royce Merlin engine on a plinth like sculpture. Colourised portraits of the airmen watching from the walls.

Darkness is a feature. Gold, oxblood, mahogany, velvet. The collection isn't shown to you; you're standing inside it.

Visual system

One look, locked across every frame

So generated footage and real product sit in the same film.

Oxblood#5A1418

Grade

Teal-lifted shadows, gold highlights, filmic contrast, soft halation and fine grain. One shared LUT across every clip.

Light & lens

Low-key, single warm motivated source; volumetric haze. 35mm for the room, 85–100mm macro for coins and hands. Shallow focus.

Motion & type

Slow, weighted moves only — dolly, push, rack focus. Inscriptional caps in gold (EB Garamond small caps), museum-placard titles.

The look, on real assets

Where we're taking it

Real product and stills, already pulled toward the new grade — beside the frames we'll generate in Flow.

The cut

Eight beats, over the voice you already approved

How we build it

The engine room

  • Google Flow (Veo) generates the environments — the gallery, the desk, the skies, the plinth, the handover.
  • Gemini animates the archive — the heroes photo, the aircraft plate, the portraits — as living photographs.
  • Real product — box, coins, Merlin relic, certificate — shot into the generated world and graded to match.
  • The VO and score stay exactly as they are. We cut the new picture to the voice you already signed off.
  • Every clip conformed, graded to one LUT, finished with grain, halation and light-bloom dissolves.

To move

What we need

  • A yes to The Keeper — or a steer, and I'll swing the whole thing.
  • Time on Flow / Gemini to generate from the prompt pack (already written, ready to run).
  • The emblem (transparent) and the final price confirmed.
  • Ideally, a clean re-export of Reg's reveal — the current copy is low-res; the real grade wants the master.

Turnaround: with clips in hand, a graded v2 cut follows quickly — same locked timeline, elevated frame by frame.
